600: Gothic Sports by Anike Hage (Tokyopop) is a spirited sports comedy from Germany. Anya transfers to Lucrece High for its strong sports program, only to clash with the girls' basketball captain and learn that the soccer team won't let girls play. So she and her friends start a soccer team of their own, complete with goth-inspired uniforms designed to draw in players. It's a fun, upbeat read for fans of underdog team stories with plenty of style.
601: Gou-Dere Sora Nagihara by Suu Minazuki (Yen Press) is a rowdy romantic comedy with a fantasy twist. Shouta Yamakawa is a manga-loving high school first-year who freezes up around girls and has fallen hard for Sora Nagihara, a character from his favorite manga. When Sora turns up in the real world, she brings nothing but chaos to his dorm and the girls in it. It's a loud, cheeky read for fans of over-the-top harem comedy.
602: The Boss by Lim Jae-won (ADV) is a brawling high school action comedy from Korea. Sang Tae Hyun is the toughest kid at Woo Sang High School, but a misdelivered note sets off a mix-up when a rival school's gang kidnaps an unpopular girl they believe is his girlfriend. One misunderstanding quickly snowballs into a string of fights. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy delinquent stories with plenty of punches and humor.
603: The Bride and the Exorcist Knight by Keiko Ishihara (Seven Seas) is a supernatural shojo romance with a touch of danger. Anne has attracted demons her whole life, and at seventeen she learns that a demon lord intends to marry her and carry her off to hell. A talented young exorcist vows to protect her, though he has feelings for her too. It's a sweet, spooky love-triangle story for fans of demon-hunting romance.
605: Hanami: International Love Story by Plus and Sung-Jae Park (Dark Horse) is a lighthearted high school romance from Korea. Hanami is a Japanese exchange student navigating life, friendship, and culture shock at a Korean school, where her feelings for a classmate named Joonho start to grow. Misunderstandings, rivals, and school events keep things lively. It's a gentle, funny read for anyone who enjoys cross-cultural school romances.
606: Najica Blitz Tactics by Takuya Tashiro (ADV) is a stylish spy action series with a sci-fi edge. By day, Najica Hiiragi is a talented perfume designer; by night, she is a skilled secret agent taking on dangerous missions. She is partnered with Lila, a humanoid android with remarkable abilities, and the two must learn to work together. It's a breezy, action-packed read for fans of the anime and of glamorous secret-agent stories.
607: Namekawa-san Won't Take a Licking! by Rie Ato (Seven Seas) is a playful yuri comedy. After years of being bullied in junior high, Namekawa-san starts high school determined to reinvent herself as a tough delinquent. Most of her classmates are scared off, but the head of the disciplinary committee is completely unfazed and keeps a close eye on her. It's a fun, teasing rivalry story for readers who like their romance with a little friction.
608: Neotopia by Rod Espinosa (Antarctic Press) is a colorful fantasy adventure in a full-color manga style. In a far future where people have traded technology for magic and legendary creatures live among humans, a servant girl named Nalyn poses as the grand duchess of the utopian city of Mathenia. When the empire of Krossos tries to kidnap her, she is swept into a war of flying ships and strange enemies. It's a bright, imaginative read for all-ages fantasy fans.
609: Nicola Traveling Around the Demons' World by Asaya Miyanaga (Seven Seas) is a gentle, whimsical fantasy adventure. Nicola is a young witch who finds herself in a world full of demons, where a devil merchant named Simon takes her under his wing. As they travel from town to town selling his wares, Nicola has to hide that she's human, all while her magic misbehaves. It's a cozy, slightly eerie read for anyone who loves a sense of wonder.
610: Nirvana by Jin and Sayuki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure about fate and second chances. Yachiyo Hitotose is a kindhearted young woman on her way overseas to work as a relief volunteer when her plane crashes. She wakes in a mystical world shaped by reincarnation and destiny, where people revere her as a goddess who stands against evil. It's an earnest, sweeping read for fans of isekai with a spiritual bent.
611: Barbarities by Tsuta Suzuki (Seven Seas) is a boys' love romance set in a Renaissance-inspired Europe. When the powerful Lord Montague needs a bodyguard, the blond Viscount Adam Canning offers his sword, with plans to enjoy a little romance on the side. He falls for Montague's nephew Joel, a serious young man devoted to fighting crime and corruption, who is not at all charmed. It's a witty, slow-burn read for BL fans who like historical intrigue.
612: High School DxD by Hiroji Mishima (Yen Press) is a racy supernatural action comedy based on the light novels by Ichiei Ishibumi. Issei Hyodo is a lovestruck high school pervert whose very first date ends with him being killed by a fallen angel. He's brought back to life by Rias Gremory, a gorgeous upperclassman who turns out to be a devil, and he wakes up as a member of her household. It's a loud, fan-service-heavy read for older fans of the anime.
614: Battle Rabbits by Yuki Amemiya and Yukino Ichihara (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action series from the creators of 07-Ghost. Kokuryuu Kaguya joins the Battle Rabbits, an organization that protects Earth from monsters, with one goal in mind: revenge on the demons who killed his father. He soon finds himself fighting alongside unusual allies. It's a fast, stylish read for fans of monster-fighting shonen.
615: The Isolator by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action story from the creator of Sword Art Online and Accel World. Minoru Utsugi is a high school student who wants nothing more than to be left alone, so when a mysterious alien seed gives him an impenetrable protective shell, it seems like a perfect fit. Soon he's recruited to fight the Ruby Eyes, dangerous beings with powers of their own. It's a moody, inventive read for fans of superpowered sci-fi.
616: Beasts of Abigaile by Spica Aoki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy shojo romance loosely inspired by Little Red Riding Hood. Nina Tsukishiro arrives in the fairy-tale country of Ruberia, where a wolf-eared young man bites her and turns her into one of the land's beasts. She is sent to Abigaile, a school-like prison for beast-people, and must keep her wits about her as she uncovers its secrets. It's a sweet, spirited read for fans of reverse-harem fantasy.
617: Because I'm the Goddess by Shamneko (Tokyopop) is a fantasy action comedy with plenty of mischief. Aoi's hometown is wiped out by a tidal wave accidentally caused by Pandora, a goddess-in-training. Now he reluctantly helps her track down the Gifts, beings that possess women and enslave men, so she can become a complete Goddess. It's a quirky, energetic read for fans of offbeat adventure.
618: Honey Mustard by Ho-Kyung Yeo (Tokyopop) is a light, funny romance from Korea. Ara has a knack for landing in awkward situations, and one of them ties her into an unexpected arrangement with Young-Woo, a boy she barely knows. Meanwhile, she still carries a torch for her first love, Jung Hanil, who doesn't feel the same. It's a sweet, messy love story for readers who enjoy romantic comedy with plenty of mix-ups.
619: Beyond the Beyond by Yoshitomo Watanabe (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure with a big heart. Futaba Kudo is a sixth grader who's small for his age, until a girl named Kiara falls from the sky with all sorts of people hunting her. He vows to protect her and help her find her missing master, and their escape through a portal pulls him into a fantasy world. It's a charming, storybook-style read for fans of classic quest tales.
620: Oninagi by Akira Ishida (Yen Press) is a supernatural action comedy. Fifteen-year-old Nanami Kushimiya finds herself targeted by Tomotaka Onigoroshi, a demon slayer who is convinced she's a demon. When Nanami destroys a tree demon with a sudden burst of power, the two discover it may come from an ancestor who married a demon. It's a quick, playful read for fans of monster-hunting stories with a light touch.
621: The Other Side of Secret by Hideaki Yoshikawa (Seven Seas) is a fantasy action series with a mysterious edge. Seven years ago, Yuuto's older sister showed him a door to another world, told him not to follow, and never came back. Now living alone with his cat, he is still searching for her when the door reappears and two sisters tumble out of it. It's a moody adventure with heavy fan service, best for older readers who enjoy portal fantasy.
622: How to Train Your Devil by Tonchi Kataoka (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy comedy with a parenting twist. A young woman wielding a magic sword is destined to champion humanity against the demons, but there's a catch: the reigning demon lord is a baby. Instead of fighting him, she ends up as his surrogate parent, trying to steer him toward good deeds. It's a cozy, funny read for anyone who enjoys found-family fantasy.
623: Black Knight by Kai Tsurugi (Blu) is a boys' love fantasy romance with courtly intrigue. Prince Christen Jeremy is a kindhearted sixteen-year-old who is sent to a knights' academy, where he meets the Black Knight Zeke. A plot to assassinate the prince is brewing, and Zeke may be the only one who can protect him. It's a dramatic, swashbuckling read for BL fans who love knights and royalty.
624: Our Teachers Are Dating! by Pikachi Ohi (Seven Seas) is a sweet, lighthearted yuri romance about grown-ups. Gym teacher Asuka Hayama and science teacher Saki Terano are dating, and when their relationship becomes obvious, the school community accepts it warmly. Most of the bumps come from two shy adults learning to talk to each other. It's a fluffy, feel-good read for fans of gentle workplace romance.
625: The Seven Princes of the Thousand-Year Labyrinth by Yu Aikawa and Haruno Atori (Seven Seas) is a fantasy mystery with a puzzle-box setup. In this kingdom, each new ruler is chosen by locking a group of young candidates inside a labyrinthine castle until one of them takes the throne. This generation's mix includes a detective and the thief he chases, a singer, a martial artist, a mathematician, and more. It's a twisty, stylish read for fans of locked-room intrigue.
626: The Two of Them Are Pretty Much Like This by Takashi Ikeda (Seven Seas) is a quiet, slice-of-life yuri romance. Ellie Sakuma, a 30-year-old scenario writer, and Wako Inuzuka, a 20-year-old voice actress, share an apartment and tell everyone they're just roommates. In truth, they're in love, and the story follows their everyday moments, from deadlines at a family restaurant to walks home together. It's a warm, low-key read for anyone who enjoys domestic romance.
627: Bound Beauty by Mick Takeuchi (Go! Comi) is a supernatural shojo drama with a darker edge. Chiyako earns money as a fortuneteller, really using her ability to see the red strings of fate, so she can escape her abusive father. When she follows her calligraphy teacher to a mysterious mansion, an accident shrinks her into a child's body and gives her the power to manipulate fate, pulling her into a group called the Tyers. It's an eerie, atmospheric read for fans of spirit-battle shojo.
628: Pearl Pink by Meca Tanaka (Tokyopop) is a bubbly shojo romantic comedy set in show business. High schooler Kanji sees a blond boy beat up some bullies, only to learn the fighter is actually Tamako, the hidden daughter of a top idol at his father's talent agency. Because her mother's career depends on keeping her a secret, Tamako moves in with Kanji and his father. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of idol stories and childhood-friend romance.
629: Peppermint by Eun-Jin Seo (Tokyopop) is a light, comedic school romance from Korea. Hey is an ordinary teenage girl with a big crush on EZ, a teen singer who attends her school and often asks her to help him rehearse. His attention earns her the wrath of his fan club, until a junior high skateboarder named EO steps in and asks her to pose as his girlfriend. It's a breezy read for fans of love triangles and celebrity crushes.
630: In Dream World by Jae-Ho Yoon (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure from Korea. In this world, nightmares are real, physical monsters, and Drake, Hanee, and Kyle fight them with weapons and In Dream Cards that grant elemental powers. Hanee and her friends must make their way through the land of Nightmares to find their way home. It's a quick, action-filled read for fans of card-powered quests.
631: Instant Teen: Just Add Nuts by Haruka Fukushima (Tokyopop) is a playful shojo comedy with a magical twist. Fifth grader Natsumi Kawashima can't wait to grow up, so when she eats some mysterious pink nuts from a mall giveaway, she wakes up in the body of a young woman. Suddenly she has to navigate a grown-up world, and grown-up feelings, while still being a kid inside. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of body-swap and wish-fulfillment stories.
632: Can't Stop Cursing You by Kensuke Koba and Natsuko Uruma (Yen Press) is a dark supernatural mystery. In this world, people who make contracts with devils gain the power to curse others to death. Curse Detective Kiyoharu Saeyama tracks the traces these curses leave behind to find the killers, setting up a tense battle of wits each time. It's a gripping read for fans of occult detective stories and psychological cat-and-mouse games.
633: This Is Screwed Up, but I Was Reincarnated as a GIRL in Another World! by Ashi and Keyaki Uchiuchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure with a clever survival streak. Ren is an orphan girl being transported after being sold when an accident brings back memories of her past life as a male researcher in his thirties. Armed with magic and scientific know-how, she sets out to survive a harsh world and escape the investor who bought her. It's a resourceful read for fans of isekai.
634: Captain Corinth by Tomomasa Takuma (One Peace Books) is a sci-fi fantasy adventure based on a popular Japanese novel series. In the far future, Captain Alan Corinth of the Imperial Navy is fighting an alien threat when a mysterious attack sends his battleship crashing onto an unknown planet. Instead of the advanced humanity he knows, he finds people living in a world of swords and magic. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy fish-out-of-water isekai.
635: Captive Hearts of Oz by Ryo Maruya (Seven Seas) is a romantic fantasy retelling of The Wonderful Wizard of Oz. Dorothy is swept away from her quiet life and lands in the strange land of Oz, where she sets out to find her way home. Along the road she meets reimagined, handsome versions of the Scarecrow, the Tin Man, and the Lion. It's a sweet, storybook read for fans of fairy-tale retellings with a shojo touch.
636: Catch These Hands! by murata (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny yuri romantic comedy about grown-ups. Takebe is a former high school delinquent who feels stuck as her old friends marry and settle down, so she looks up her old rival, Soramori, for a rematch. Soramori agrees on one condition: if she wins, Takebe has to date her. It's a dry, charming slow burn for readers who like romance about finding your place as an adult.
637: Jazz by Sakae Maeda and Tamotsu Takamure (DMP) is a tender boys' love drama. Naoki is a young man whose illness weighs heavily on his daily life, and over time he falls in love with his caretaker, Dr. Koichi Naruwasa. The story follows whether Koichi can, or will, return those feelings. It's a heartfelt read for BL fans who enjoy quiet, emotional romance.
638: Cherry Juice by Haruka Fukushima (Tokyopop) is a sweet shojo romance with a family twist. Otoha and Kanata grew up as close childhood friends, but when their parents marry, they become stepsiblings under the same roof. Otoha is determined to keep the peace at home, even as her feelings for Kanata grow complicated. It's a gentle, heartfelt read for fans of slow-blooming school romance.
639: Portrait of M & N by Tachibana Higuchi (Tokyopop) is a quirky shojo romantic comedy. Mitsuru is a graceful, admired student with a secret masochistic streak, and Natsuhiko, who discovers it on their first day of high school, has his own problem: one glimpse of his reflection sends him into raptures over his own beauty. Both are desperate to keep their quirks hidden. It's a silly, offbeat read for fans of oddball comedy romance.
640: Chocolat by Ji-Sang Shin and Geo (Ice Kunion) is a lively romantic comedy from Korea set in the world of pop music fandom. Kum-ji is a devoted fan of the band DDL, but she misses her chance to join their fan club. When she learns that Yo-I, a newer band, is DDL's rival, she joins Yo-I's fan club just to get closer to her idols, and keeping that secret quickly gets complicated. It's a fun pick for anyone who loves idol stories.
641: Psy-Comm by Jason Henderson and Tony Salvaggio (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi action series with a sharp satirical edge. In the near future, nations have given way to corporate city-states and war has become entertainment, starring genetically altered psychic commandos called Psy-Comms. Mark Leit is expected to become the greatest Psy-Comm ever, until a tragedy in his past drives him to walk away, which his best friend sees as betrayal. It's a fast read for fans of media-satire sci-fi.
642: Core Scramble by Euho Jun (Net Comics) is a Korean romance with a supernatural action thread. Chaeun finds herself growing attached to Moonhoo, only to discover that Moonhoo is a Core Hunter. Meanwhile, tension is building between the people who create mysterious holes and the people who fight them, and the two find themselves caught in the middle. It's a quick read for fans of romance mixed with otherworldly conflict.
644: Qwan by Aki Shimizu (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure steeped in Chinese myth. Qwan is a mysterious boy with an unusual appetite: he eats demons. He travels across ancient China alongside a scholar named Tenshou, and their journey brings them face to face with all sorts of strange and dangerous creatures. It's an imaginative, beautifully drawn read for fans of mythic journeys and supernatural action.
645: Crown of Love by Yun Kouga (Viz Media) is a shojo drama set in the glittering world of show business. Sixteen-year-old Hisayoshi "Kumi" Tajima has never cared about romance until a chance collision with teen idol Rima Fujio leaves him smitten. With no ordinary way to see her again, he jumps at the chance when her former agent offers to make him an idol too. The catch is that Rima sees him as a rival. It's a great pick for fans of idol stories.
646: Ugly Duckling's Love Revolution by Yuuki Fujinari (Yen Press) is a bubbly shojo romantic comedy. Hitomi Sakuragawa is chubby and clumsy, and she happens to live next door to the five popular boys who rule Saint Leaf School. When they take her under their wing, she starts working out and slowly gaining confidence. It's a silly, upbeat makeover story for readers who enjoy reverse-harem school comedy.
647: Kiss the Scars of the Girls by Aya Haruhana (Yen Press) is a gothic yuri drama with a supernatural twist. On her fourteenth birthday, a young vampire named Emille is given a "Big Sister" to teach her how to survive. As the two hunt and feed together, Emille begins to wonder whether their bond could become something more. It's a moody, romantic read for fans of vampire stories and classic sisterhood yuri.
648: Cutie and the Beast by Yuhi Azumi (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted romantic comedy with a pro-wrestling twist. While her friends swoon over pretty boys, high schooler Momoka has a crush on Kuga, a towering professional wrestler who plays a villain on TV. Off-screen, though, Kuga turns out to be gentle and touched by her fan mail. It's a sweet, funny read for anyone who loves an unlikely romance.
649: Cy-Believers by Shioko Mizuki (Go! Comi) is a zany school comedy with a sci-fi edge. At the Domus Aurea boarding school, an elite student government rules with an iron fist, and Rui walks away from her controlling fiancé, the head of the Public Safety Commission. Assigned to a scrappy club of misfits, she ends up founding a computer club as hints emerge that a mysterious computer may be running the school. It's an exaggerated, goofy read for fans of school-power-struggle comedy.
650: Dance in the Vampire Bund II: Scarlet Order by Nozomu Tamaki (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action series set in the world of Dance in the Vampire Bund. Vampire queen Mina Tepes holds two fragments of the akamitama, a relic said to let even a vampire live without feeding, and several rival factions are hunting the remaining pieces. As a familiar face returns to the Bund offering information, Mina struggles with the stone's effects. It's a must for fans of the original series.
651: Danganronpa 2: Ultimate Luck and Hope and Despair, based on the game by Spike Chunsoft (Dark Horse), is a tense mystery thriller based on the hit video game. Hajime Hinata arrives at the elite Hope's Peak Academy, only to find himself and his talented classmates stranded on a tropical island. Their cheerful getaway quickly turns into a deadly game where the only way off the island is to get away with murder. It's a twisty, darkly funny read for fans of the games and of killing-game mysteries.
652: Red Hot Chili Samurai by Yoshitsugu Katagiri (Tokyopop) is a goofy samurai comedy. Its hero is a capable swordsman with an unusual weakness: he's hooked on hot peppers and is miserable without them. He roams a loosely historical Japan, dispensing justice in short, episodic adventures with a quirky supporting cast, including a ninja who talks by holding up signs. It's a light, silly read for fans of offbeat period comedy.
653: Hatsune Miku: Rin-chan Now! by Hiroshi Itaba (Dark Horse) is a playful slice-of-life comedy starring Vocaloid star Kagamine Rin. Inspired by the hit music video of the same name, it follows Hatsune Miku's sassy blond friend through everyday antics. Light and silly from start to finish, it's a fun, upbeat read for Vocaloid fans and anyone who enjoys short, character-driven comedy.
654: Virgin Love by Tina Yamashina (Kodansha) is a grown-up romance about second chances. Shoko Shoji is a 26-year-old professional who seems to have it all, but she's quietly embarrassed that she has never been in a relationship. She joins the Love House, an experimental shared home where six single people look for romance under one roof, while an old heartbreak still lingers. It's a heartfelt read for fans of reality-show-style romance.
655: Visitor by Yi-Jung No (Tokyopop) is a Korean drama with a strong horror streak. Everyone Hyo-Bin has grown close to has been brutally murdered, and the horror follows her into nightmares filled with classmates from her new school. As she tries to make new friends and maybe find romance, she also starts developing a supernatural ability she can neither understand nor control. It's an eerie, gripping read for fans of supernatural mysteries.
656: WaqWaq by Ryu Fujisaki (Viz Media) is a post-apocalyptic fantasy adventure from the creator of Hoshin Engi. In a future where humans live in fear of hostile creatures called machines, twelve-year-old Shio becomes a Guardian, a warrior with supernatural powers, after his father dies. He sets out with Matsuda, a red-blooded girl believed to be a god, toward the Spider's Thread, a device said to grant any wish. It's an inventive quest story for shonen fans.
657: Warriors of Tao by Shinya Kuwahara (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi fantasy action series with a deadly twist. Ordinary high school student Toma Suguri is chosen to fight for Earth in an interplanetary tournament where the losers literally become food. In this universe, one world feeds on another, and only a single planet will survive. It's an intense, high-stakes read for fans of tournament battles.
658: Rose Hip Zero by Tohru Fujisawa (Tokyopop) is a hard-hitting action thriller from the creator of Great Teacher Onizuka. A mysterious terrorist group called ALICE is recruiting teenagers as killers, and detective Kyoji Shima is assigned to protect Kasumi Kitami, a schoolgirl who may hold the key to stopping it. Kasumi is far tougher than she looks. It's a fast, gritty read for fans of gunfights and cop drama.
659: Deep Scar by Rossella Sergi (Tokyopop) is a contemporary romance drama with a mysterious undercurrent. Shy, quiet Sofia moves to Turin for school, leaving her family and her boyfriend Luca behind for the first time. Her new roommate Veronica lives a very different lifestyle, and an enigmatic young man named Lorenzo seems a little too interested in Sofia. It's an emotional read for fans of slow-burn romance with a darker edge.
660: Sabrina the Teenage Witch: The Magic Within by Tania Del Rio (Archie Comics) is a playful magical comedy drawn in a manga style. Sabrina Spellman is a teenager trying to balance an ordinary high school life with her secret magical one, all while dealing with friends, crushes, and the occasional supernatural mishap. This version gives the classic character a fresh, shojo-inspired spin. It's a fun, lighthearted read for longtime Sabrina fans and newcomers alike.
661: Welcome to the Outcast's Restaurant! by Tsumumi (Kaiten Books) is a cozy fantasy comedy about food and fresh starts. Dennis is a level 99 chef who gets kicked out of the powerful adventuring party he cooked for. Instead of moping, he opens a restaurant in a small town, serving hearty meals to adventurers and regulars, along with a fellow outcast who joins him. It's a warm, appetizing read for fans of slice-of-life fantasy and cooking stories.
662: World End Solte by Satoshi Mizukami (Seven Seas) is a fantasy adventure from the creator of Planet With. In a world scarred by war, magical pollution warps time and space. Solte is an orphan whose parents died trying to cleanse it, but rather than follow in their footsteps exactly, she dives into the pollution like a treasure-seeking Salvager, determined to reach the other side and find answers. It's an imaginative read for fans of exploration fantasy.
663: World Piece by Josh Tierney and Agroshka (Viz Media) is a lively sci-fi fantasy adventure. High school basketball player Lucas Densen accidentally activates an ancient alien artifact at one of his mom's archaeological digs, and it shrinks Earth down to a glowing orb the size of a basketball. Transported to a realm of palm-sized worlds, he teams up with a friendly alien named Lully to find a way to set things right. It's a fun, colorful read for all-ages adventure fans.
664: Destiny's Hand by Nunzio DeFilippis and Christina Weir (Seven Seas) is a swashbuckling pirate adventure. Olivia Soldana escapes an arranged marriage by joining Captain Sebastian Blaine's crew, trading a life of comfort for one on the high seas. When the captain is badly wounded by a rival pirate, he names Olivia to lead the crew on a quest for the legendary Devil's Eye. It's a brisk, fun read for fans of high-seas action with a strong heroine.
665: Sakurai-san Wants to Be Noticed by Akinosora (Seven Seas) is a sweet, teasing school romantic comedy. Mako would like nothing more than to spend his afternoons relaxing in class, but his popular classmate Sakurai keeps interrupting his peace. Is she flirting with him, or is he just reading too much into it? It's a cute, low-stakes read for fans of will-they-won't-they romance.
666: Do Whatever You Want by Yeri Na (Net Comics) is a thoughtful Korean drama about friendship and ambition. Jiwon and Hosoo are high school best friends who dream of musical stardom and have sworn to chase it together, ahead of everything else. Rumors swirl that they're more than friends, but both are wrestling with family troubles and big goals of their own. It's a heartfelt read for fans of coming-of-age stories about music and loyalty.
667: Doughnuts Under a Crescent Moon by Shio Usui (Seven Seas) is a quiet, thoughtful yuri romance about grown-ups. Uno Hinako tries hard to seem normal to her friends and coworkers, focusing on makeup, fashion, and dating men, but none of it ever quite fits. Her friendship with Asahi Sato, a sensible coworker, slowly becomes her new normal and grows into something deeper. It's a gentle, honest read for anyone who enjoys realistic workplace romance.
668: Yashakiden: The Demon Princess by Hideyuki Kikuchi (DMP) is a dark supernatural horror novel set in Demon City Shinjuku. Ever since the Devil Quake, Shinjuku has been a sordid haven for the paranormal, where demons and humans live in an uneasy balance. When four ancient Chinese vampires arrive to seize the city, the elegant private investigator Setsura Aki and the demon physician Doctor Mephisto must set aside their rivalry and work together. It's a moody, gory read for fans of Kikuchi's Vampire Hunter D.
670: Madtown Hospital by JTK (Net Comics) is a wacky Korean comedy set in a hospital full of oddballs. Dr. Don seems to make every patient sicker, and Nurse Lee is a former supermodel who has fallen from fame. Together with the rest of the eccentric staff, they turn every shift into chaos. It's a quick, silly read for anyone who enjoys absurd workplace humor.
671: Maico 2010 by Toshimitsu Shimizu (Comics One) is a lighthearted sci-fi comedy. In the year 2010, a struggling radio station unveils its newest DJ: Maico, a cheerful android with a big personality. As she tries to win over listeners and learn about the humans around her, misadventures follow. It's a breezy, playful read for fans of the anime and of robot-girl comedies.
672: Zero's Familiar: Chevalier by Noboru Yamaguchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy that continues the story of The Familiar of Zero. Louise, a bumbling witch-in-training, is still magically bound to Saito, the ordinary teenage boy she accidentally summoned from Earth as her familiar. This series follows the pair into new adventures, with Yukari Higa's art bringing the light novels to life. It's a fun pick for fans of the original series and its anime.
673: E's by Satoru Yuiga (Broccoli Books) is a sci-fi action drama about people with psychic powers. Kai Kudou is an Esper recruited by the organization Ashurum, which claims to protect psychics from ordinary humans. After a mission goes wrong, he begins to question Ashurum's true goals while worrying about his ill sister, who is in the organization's care. It's an earnest, action-filled read for fans of the E's Otherwise anime.
675: Evergreen by Yuyuko Takemiya and Akira Kasukabe (Seven Seas) is a sweet school romantic comedy from the author of Toradora! Hotaka Yoshimatsu is a shy teen and president of his school's manga club, and he has a crush on Niki Awaya, a talented swimmer. When his coach insists he swim for a qualifying test, he has to face his self-consciousness about the scar on his chest from a heart operation. It's a gentle, funny read for fans of awkward first love.
676: May These Leaden Battlegrounds Leave No Trace by Kei Uekawa (Yen Press) is a sci-fi military fantasy light novel. For a century, the East and West have fought a brutal war with everything from tanks to witchcraft. Young Eastern soldier Rain Lantz discovers a handful of mysterious silver bullets that erase their targets from both the battlefield and history, then meets their creator, a Ghost named Air, who warns him that using them to end the war will cost him his freedom. It's a gripping read for war-story fans.
677: Fairy Girls by Boku, based on Hiro Mashima's Fairy Tail (Kodansha), is a lighthearted fantasy action spinoff. Erza, Lucy, and Wendy team up to take on guild jobs together, from monster hunts to stranger requests. Each adventure is a chance for the three to show off their magic and their friendship. It's a fun, breezy read for Fairy Tail fans who love its heroines.
678: Fiancée of the Wizard by Syuri Nakamura and Masaki Kazuka (Yen Press) is a sweet shojo fantasy romance adapted from a light novel. A woman is reborn as a young girl in a world of swords and sorcery, where she crosses paths with the strikingly handsome but grumpy son of a wizard. What follows is a mix of magic, adventure, and slowly growing affection. It's a charming read for fans of gentle isekai romance.
679: Shaolin Sisters: Reborn by Narumi Kakinouchi (Tokyopop) is a martial arts fantasy action series and a follow-up to Shaolin Sisters. Three sisters, Seilin, Kalin, and Julin Kenga, learn they are the reincarnations of an ancient martial arts clan that once saved the world. As strange figures begin to appear around them, Julin starts to understand her heritage and the battles ahead. It's a fast, action-first read for fans of kung fu fantasy.
680: Shrine of the Morning Mist by Hiroki Ugawa (Tokyopop) is a supernatural romantic comedy steeped in Shinto folklore. High school freshman Yuzu Hieda is one of three sisters who serve as shrine maidens at their local shrine. When her childhood love returns to town, dark gods take an interest in him, and Yuzu rallies her classmates into a Miko Council to fight back. It's a charming, spirited read for fans of the anime and of shrine-maiden adventures.
681: Since I Could Die Tomorrow by Sumako Kari (Tokyopop) is a thoughtful, gently humorous slice-of-life story about growing older. Satsuki is a woman in her mid-forties who starts wondering what would happen if she died tomorrow. Those thoughts lead her to reflect on her family, her health, her friendships, and the small joys of everyday life. It's a warm, relatable read for adult readers who enjoy quiet, honest stories.
682: The Otherworlder, Exploring the Dungeon by Hinagi Asami (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel. Short on money, Souya takes a sketchy job that sends him to a fantasy world with a team of specialists to climb a dungeon tower and steal its treasure, but a malfunction strands him there alone. To survive, he gathers an unlikely group of allies, including exiled elven sisters and a goddess who prefers lounging around as a cat. It's a fun read for fans of dungeon-crawling isekai.
683: Mobile Suit Gundam SEED Astray R by Tomohiro Chiba and Yasunari Toda (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi mecha action series set in the Gundam SEED universe. In Cosmic Era 71, space is full of scavengers, thieves, and pirates. Lowe Guele, a skilled junk-tech mechanic, has come into possession of a secret mobile suit, and plenty of dangerous people want it for themselves. It's a fast, gear-packed read for Gundam fans who love the side stories.
684: The Dark-Hunters by Sherrilyn Kenyon (St. Martin's Griffin) is a paranormal romance adaptation of the bestselling novel series. Amanda Devereaux is a sensible accountant who wants nothing to do with her family's supernatural business, until she wakes up handcuffed to Kyrian of Thrace, an ancient Greek warrior turned immortal vampire hunter. Together they must face a deadly enemy. It's a fun, romantic read for fans of the novels.
686: Tiger and Dragon by Mizuki Hoshino (Seven Seas) is a sweet shojo romance about childhood friends. Konomi's best friend Kagetora moved away when they were five, and after ten years without a word, she has decided to let go of her crush. Her other childhood friend, Tatsuomi, seems more than ready to step in, until Kagetora suddenly comes back and throws her love life into chaos. It's a fun, fluttery read for fans of love triangles.
688: The Ancient Magus' Bride: Jack Flash and the Faerie Case Files by Yu Godai and Mako Oikawa, supervised by Kore Yamazaki (Seven Seas), is a fantasy mystery spinoff. The story moves from the English countryside to New York City, where a hidden magical world thrives unnoticed. Jack, a changeling fae left in the human world, and Larry, a human raised among magic who can turn into a wolf, team up to solve crimes that cross between realms. It's a charming read for fans of the original series.
689: Breakfast with My Two-Tailed Cat by Ai Shimizu (Seven Seas) is a gentle, cozy slice-of-life story with a touch of folklore. Souichiro and his wife moved to the countryside to live the quiet life they'd always dreamed of, but soon after, she passes away. His devoted cat Nii transforms into a nekomata, a two-tailed cat spirit, to keep him company, and the two spend their days cooking and enjoying nature together. It's a warm, quietly moving read for fans of food manga and healing stories.
691: World of Warcraft: Legends (Tokyopop) is a fantasy anthology set in the world of Azeroth. Each volume collects short stories from different writers and artists, including Richard A. Knaak, exploring heroes, villains, and corners of the Warcraft universe. The tales range from epic battles to more personal adventures. It's a great pick for Warcraft players and fans of the game's lore.
692: RWBY: Official Manga Anthology (Viz Media) is a collection of short stories set in the world of Remnant. Japanese artists put their own spin on Ruby, Weiss, Blake, and Yang, along with friends from the hit animated series, in tales that range from action-packed to silly. Each volume puts the spotlight on a different member of the team. It's a fun, varied read for RWBY fans who want more time with the team.
693: The Invincible Shovel by Yasohachi Tsuchise (Seven Seas) is a comedic fantasy light novel. Alan is the world's strongest miner, able to level mountains with his legendary shovel, which also happens to make him immortal. He teams up with a princess who has run away from home, and together they hunt for cursed jewels and try to save her kingdom from an invading demon army. It's a goofy, good-natured read for fans of RPG-style fantasy.
694: The NPCs in This Village Sim Game Must Be Real! by Hirukuma (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy story with a twist. Yoshio is a shut-in who passes his days playing a village-building simulation game. But the villagers he's looking after seem to be real people in another world, and his choices in the game have real consequences for them. It's a heartwarming read for fans of gentle isekai and village-building stories.
696: Woof Woof Story by Inumajin (Yen Press) is a lighthearted fantasy comedy light novel. A man worked to exhaustion in his past life wishes to be reborn as a pampered house dog, and he does get reborn as a dog, just not the kind he expected: a Fenrir, a legendary and fearsome wolf. All he really wants is to be a lazy pet, but his power keeps getting him into trouble. It's a fun, easygoing read for isekai fans.
697: Boogiepop Doesn't Laugh by Kouhei Kadono (Seven Seas) is a manga adaptation of the landmark light novel. Students at a Japanese high school whisper about Boogiepop, a mysterious figure said to appear when someone is in danger. As girls begin to disappear, several students' stories intersect around the legend. It's a moody, intriguing read for fans of psychological mystery and urban legends.
698: Chasing After Aoi Koshiba by Hazuki Takeoka and Fly (Kodansha) is a wistful yuri romance about first love. At a reunion, Sahoko is disappointed that Aoi Koshiba, her first love, isn't there. Back in school, Sahoko pursued Aoi mostly for her status as a star basketball player, but after Aoi quit the team, a kiss pulled them into something closer than Sahoko expected. It's a bittersweet, emotional read for fans of Bloom Into You.
699: Nosatsu Junkie by Ryoko Fukuyama (Tokyopop) is a lively shojo romantic comedy set in the modeling world. After her crush rejects her for not smiling like a flower, Naka Kaburagi joins a modeling agency to get revenge. There she discovers that her rival, the popular model Umi Kajiwara, is secretly a boy, and Umi makes her his co-model to keep her quiet. It's a funny, stylish read for fans of secret-identity romance.
700: Bloody Sweet by NaRae Lee (Yen Press) is a full-color Korean romance with a gentle gothic edge. Naerim is an eighteen-year-old high schooler worn down by relentless bullying when she accidentally awakens Fetechou, a centuries-old vampire. He becomes an unexpected source of comfort, though he has his own reasons for staying close: her unusually powerful blood could help him become human again. It suits readers who like tender vampire romance with real emotional weight.
701: Portrait of M&N by Tachibana Higuchi (Tokyopop) is a lively shojo romantic comedy from the creator of Gakuen Alice. A high school girl hiding an embarrassing masochistic streak crosses paths with a handsome classmate who can't stop admiring his own reflection. Once they discover each other's secrets, the two form an awkward alliance to keep them hidden. It's light, silly fun for readers who enjoy offbeat school comedies and bickering, slow-building romance.
703: Absolute Duo by Shinichirou Nariie (Seven Seas) is an action fantasy set at a school for students with supernatural weapons. At Koryo Academy, students manifest Blazes, weapons drawn from their own souls, and Tooru Kokonoe is the odd one out when his Blaze takes the form of a shield. He is paired with Julie, a quiet transfer student from Northern Europe, as academy partners. It's a good fit for fans of battle-school stories with a touch of romance.
705: The Villainess Turns The Hourglass by Sansobee (Ize Press) is a full-color fantasy of second chances and revenge. Aria spent her first life as a scheming noble daughter, only to be outmaneuvered by her sweet-faced half-sister and sent to her death. When a mysterious hourglass sends her back in time, she resolves to play the game smarter and turn the tables. It's for readers who enjoy clever, determined heroines and satisfying palace intrigue.
706: The Knight Captain is the New Princess-To-Be by Yasuko Yamaru (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy romantic comedy. Christina, known as Lady Chris, was raised much like a boy and now serves as captain of the imperial guard, protecting her childhood friend, Prince Leonardo. When the king tells Leo to choose a wife, he announces he's already picked Chris, and she plays along, assuming it's all for show. It's a charming read for fans of fake-engagement romance and capable heroines.
707: Tengen Hero Wars by Yasu Hiromoto and Kubara Sakanoichi (Titan Manga) is a high-energy historical fantasy adventure. A modern teen named Oda Nobunaga, mocked for his obsession with history, is pulled into the past while trying to save his little sister, who is then taken by bandits. With no special powers, he has only his encyclopedic knowledge of historical figures to offer the warlord who shares his name. It's great for readers who love famous figures from Japanese history thrown together in big battles.
708: Plum Crazy! Tales of a Tiger-Striped Cat by Natsumi Hoshino (Seven Seas) is a gentle, all-ages comedy about life with cats. Plum is a tiger-striped cat living with the Nakarai family, sharing the household with other feline friends, including a mischievous kitten named Snowball. Short chapters follow everyday cat antics, naps, and small household adventures. It's a cozy pick for cat lovers and readers who enjoy warm slice-of-life stories.
709: It's All Your Fault by merryhachi (Yen Press) is a lively yuri comedy set in the world of cosplay. Shiho Kumai, a devoted manga fan and cosplayer, steps in to help a woman being harassed at her university, who turns out to be Yotogi, a popular cosplayer with a huge online following. After they team up at an event, Shiho learns that Yotogi's revealing style is exactly the kind of cosplay she dislikes. It's a fun pick for readers who enjoy fandom stories and sparky, mismatched pairs.
711: Psy Come by Mizuki Mizushiro (Yen Press) is a darkly comic action light novel. Kyousuke Kamiya is an ordinary teenager until he's wrongly convicted of murdering twelve people and shipped off to Purgatorium, a reform school for juvenile killers. Surrounded by classmates who really are dangerous, he just wants to survive and keep his head down. It's for readers who like twisted school settings, black humor, and over-the-top characters.
712: Telepathic Wanderers by Yasutaka Tsutsui and Sayaka Yamazaki (Tokyopop) is a psychological thriller with supernatural elements. Based on Tsutsui's novel Nanase Futatabi, it follows Nanase, a young woman who can hear other people's thoughts and has learned to keep her gift hidden. As she travels, she meets others with unusual powers of their own and learns how dangerous it can be to be found out. It's for readers who enjoy quiet, unsettling stories about psychic abilities.
713: StarCraft: Frontline by Various Authors (Tokyopop) is an anthology of science fiction manga set in Blizzard's StarCraft universe. Each volume gathers several self-contained stories from different creators, following Terran soldiers, Protoss warriors, and the ever-present Zerg threat. The tales range from frontline combat to smaller, character-driven moments in a galaxy at war. It's a natural fit for fans of the games and readers who like gritty military sci-fi in short doses.
714: Cells at Work! Baby by Akane Shimizu (Kodansha) is a cheerful educational comedy, drawn by Yasuhiro Fukuda, set inside the body of a newborn. The baby's cells are just as new to their jobs as the baby is to the world, and every hiccup, feeding, and first germ becomes a big event. Like the original series, it explains real biology through lovable, hardworking characters. It's a fun read for fans of Cells at Work! and curious readers of all ages.
715: I See Your Face, Turned Away by Rumi Ichinohe (Kodansha) is a bittersweet school romance from the creator of My Sweet Girl. It follows four teenagers and four stories of unrequited love, each watching the person they care about from a distance. They want to protect their friendships, but they can't stop hoping for something more. It's a lovely fit for readers who enjoy quiet, emotional romance like A Sign of Affection.
718: My Beautiful Man by Nagira Yuu (Yen Press) is a tender, intense boys' love romance. Hira is a quiet high schooler with a stutter who sits at the bottom of his class's social ladder. He becomes utterly devoted to Kiyoi, the aloof, beautiful boy at the very top, and the two begin an unlikely and complicated connection. It's for readers who like character-driven BL with plenty of emotional push and pull.
720: Tales of the Hundred Monsters Next Door by Yoshiko Watanuki (Seven Seas) is a gently eerie supernatural romance. Jinpachi Katagiri is a quiet book cover designer who likes his life predictable, until mysterious supernatural creatures start taking an interest in him. His strange encounters only multiply after he meets Oriza Harada, a writer known as "Ghost Sensei." Caught between his growing attraction to Harada and his wish for an ordinary life, Jinpachi finds his days anything but dull.
729: Lovely Muco! by Takayuki Mizushina (Kodansha) is a cheerful comedy about a dog and the person she adores. Muco is an energetic, endlessly affectionate little dog who lives in a small mountain town with her owner, Komatsu. Short, upbeat chapters follow her enthusiastic misadventures and her total devotion to her human, misunderstandings and all. It's an easy, feel-good read for dog lovers and fans of light slice-of-life humor.
730: The White Mage Doesn't Want To Raise The Hero's Level by Kirie (Seven Seas) is a playful isekai romantic comedy. Izumi Irie is summoned to another world as its hero and teams up with Sheena, a powerful white mage. Sheena has fallen for him and worries he'll be sent home once the Demon King is beaten, so she does everything she can to keep him distracted from leveling up. It's light, flirty fun with a healthy dose of fanservice.
733: Mii-Chan Wants To Be Kept by Waka Takase (Seven Seas) is a sweet, offbeat romantic comedy. Iori is worn out from work and still grieving his late pet cat when he takes in a stray black cat one night. The next morning, he finds a young woman in his apartment who calls herself Mii-chan and insists she's that very same cat. It's a cozy, funny read for anyone who enjoys quirky domestic romcoms and feline charm.
735: Centuria by Tohru Kuramori (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy adventure with a strong emotional core. Julian is a young boy who escapes a cruel past by stowing away on a ship, only to be discovered and made a slave himself. Among the enslaved passengers he finds an unexpected found family, especially a kind, pregnant woman named Mira. It's a gripping read for fans of grim, sweeping fantasy in the vein of Berserk and Vinland Saga.
738: Hima-Ten! by Genki Ono (Viz Media) is a lighthearted shonen romantic comedy. Tenichi Iemori is a hardworking sixteen-year-old who cleans houses part-time to help support his family. On the first day of his second year, he discovers that Himari Yoshino, the popular model who just transferred to his school, is the client whose wildly messy apartment he's been hired to clean. It's breezy fun for readers who enjoy secret-sharing romcoms with plenty of heart.
743: The Tale of a Little Alchemist Blessed by the Spirits by Yocco and Junsui (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy light novel about a fresh start. In her past life, Daisy was abandoned by her family after receiving the humble God Occupation of Maid. Reborn as a viscount's daughter, she fears history will repeat itself when she's named an Alchemist, but this time her loving family builds her a laboratory instead. It's a gentle read for fans of slow-life fantasy, found warmth, and crafting magic.
744: Futari Switch by Akira Hiramoto (Yen Press) is a body-swap comedy from the creator of Prison School. High schoolers Ichigo and Shinichi suddenly find themselves living in each other's bodies, with no idea why it happened or how to undo it. Juggling each other's friends, reputations, and secrets leads to plenty of chaos. It's a good fit for readers who enjoy Hiramoto's bold, over-the-top humor and expressive art.
745: The Tale of a Little Alchemist Blessed by the Spirits by Yocco, Asanaya, and Junsui (Seven Seas) is a sweet fantasy manga adapted from the light novel. Daisy's previous life ended in neglect after her family rejected her for receiving the God Occupation of Maid. Reborn as a viscount's daughter with the Alchemist occupation, she braces for the worst, only to find her new family eager to support her dreams. It's a warm pick for readers who love gentle, slow-life fantasy.
746: Isekai Samurai by Keigo Saito (Yen Press) is an action fantasy with a refreshingly unusual heroine. Ginko is a female samurai who survived the Battle of Sekigahara and has spent years searching for a warrior strong enough to give her an honorable death in battle. While praying for a worthy opponent, she's transported to a fantasy world where humanity is under siege by a Demon King's forces. It's a treat for readers who love sharp swordplay and a deadpan, single-minded lead.
748: Shinobi Undercover by Ippon Takegushi and Santa Mitarashi (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy with a sweet romantic streak. Yodaka is a supremely skilled ninja who happens to have crippling social anxiety. He's assigned to secretly guard Aoi Mukai, a clumsy high school girl targeted by rogue ninja, which means blending into school life and learning to actually talk to people. It's a fun mix of slick fight scenes and awkward, heartfelt comedy.
750: Taika's Reason by Paru Itagaki (Viz Media) is a dark, unsettling drama from the creator of Beastars. In a Japan where science can turn animals into humans, Ao comes home to find her family's pit bull, Taika, standing over her father's body, and she chooses to hide the truth rather than let the dog be put down. When Taika is later humanized and can finally speak, the secret they share grows even heavier. It's for readers who like tense, morally tangled stories.
754: Ultimate Exorcist Kiyoshi by Shoichi Usui (Viz Media) is a shonen action comedy about demon hunting. Kiyoshi Harai lost his parents to demons as a child and grew into an incredibly powerful exorcist, though he is painfully shy. He's assigned to an outpost in Naraku City, hidden inside a Chinese restaurant, where he battles demons alongside his fellow exorcists. It's a great pick for readers who like big supernatural fights balanced with goofy humor.
760: Spacewalking With You by Inuhiko Doronoda (Kodansha) is a warm, quietly moving coming-of-age drama. Yamato Kobayashi is a high schooler struggling with school and his part-time job, drifting close to becoming a delinquent. Everything starts to shift when he befriends Keisuke Uno, an eccentric transfer student who lives by his own set of rules. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy heartfelt friendship stories about people who see the world a little differently.
761: Love at First Memory by Narumi Hasegaki (Kodansha) is a shojo romance with a mystery at its heart. After a car accident, heiress Mia Takanashi wakes up in the hospital with no memory of her past. Soon she's approached by four different young men, each claiming to be her fiancé. It's a fun, swoony read for fans of reverse-harem romance who also like a puzzle to solve.
764: My Noisy Roommate: The Roof Over My Head Comes With Monsters by Kaho Ozaki (Kodansha) is a lighthearted supernatural comedy with a dash of romance. Osuke is excited to live on his own, until he's kicked out of his new apartment on day one. A real estate agent offers him a better place with a few conditions, including sharing it with Nijio, a striking blond man who insists that ghosts are real and that Osuke is a magnet for them. It's a fun mix of spooky and sweet.
768: Betrothed to My Sister's Ex Light Novel by Tobirano and Mai Murasaki (Seven Seas) is a tender fantasy romance. Marie has spent her life neglected by parents who adore her sister Anastasia. On her birthday she slips away to the garden and meets Duke Kyros, who is drawn to her gentle nature, and a mix-up over names sends his proposal her way. It's a satisfying read for fans of Cinderella-style stories about a quiet heroine learning her own worth.
771: Spider-Man: Octo-Girl by Hideyuki Furuhashi and Betten Court (Viz Media) is a playful action comedy set in the Spider-Man universe. After a battle with Spider-Man leaves Doctor Octopus in a coma, he wakes up in the body of Otoha Okutamiya, a middle school girl in Tokyo, with his own mind still intact. The result is a funny, surprising twist on a classic Marvel villain. It's a fun pick for Marvel fans and readers who enjoy offbeat superhero stories.
772: The Mortifying Ordeal of Being Seen by mmk (Viz Media) is a playful school romantic comedy. After a seating change, classmates Ikezawa and Eguchi end up sitting side by side. When he can't help commenting on her snug blouse, she fires right back about his own neckline, and the two settle into a running game of teasing and flustering each other. It's a fun read for fans of push-and-pull romcoms like Teasing Master Takagi-san.
776: Drawing From Your Memory by Shiki Kawabata (Kodansha) is a moving time-slip story about grief, art, and love, from the creator of Switched. Mahoro is an award-winning manga artist whose hit series was built on ideas from the notebook of Yukishima, a high school manga club classmate who died months after they met. When she gets a chance to go back, she sets out to give him back his story and save his life. It's for readers who love bittersweet, emotional romance.
778: Digimon by Akiyoshi Hongo (Tokyopop) is a fun, kid-friendly adventure based on the hit anime. A group of kids at summer camp are suddenly swept away into the Digital World, a strange land full of creatures called Digimon. Each child is paired with a Digimon partner, and together they must work as a team to survive and find their way home. It's a nostalgic pick for longtime fans and a great choice for young readers.
780: Splatoon 3 Splatlands by Sankichi Hinodeya (Viz Media) is a bright, goofy gag comedy set in the world of Nintendo's Splatoon 3. Inklings and Octolings dive into the Splatlands for colorful turf battles, silly rivalries, and plenty of over-the-top antics. The chapters are short, punchy, and packed with nods to the game. It's a natural fit for young gamers and Splatoon fans of any age.
793: Sunbeams in the Sky by Monika Kaname (Yen Press) is a gentle shojo romance about starting over. Twin sisters Himari and Mio begin high school carrying a secret they're determined to keep hidden, and Himari is still struggling with fears from her past. As they grow closer to classmates Tsukiyono and Asaka, keeping that secret gets harder. It's a heartfelt read for fans of soft, emotional school romance with themes of healing.
797: Minami Nanami Wants to Shine by Yuki Yaku (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy spin-off of Bottom-Tier Character Tomozaki, drawn by Bana Yoshida with character designs by Fly. It centers on Minami Nanami, the cheerful, energetic classmate who wants to find a way to truly shine. As she takes on new challenges, she leans on Tomozaki's help to take herself seriously. It's a fun companion read for Tomozaki fans who want more of its bright supporting cast.
